parsing_res_list.block_content: Problem:Determine the gas pressure-time loading inside a cubicle, with a small vent opening, due to an internal explosion. The vent opening may be sealed or unsealed with a frangible panel or cover.
Step 1.Apply a 20% factor of safety to the charge weight.
Step 2.Calculate the free volume inside the cubicle Vf.
Step 3.Determine the charge weight to free volume ratio $W/V_{f}.$
Step 4.Determine the peak gas pressure $P_{g}$ from Figure 2-152 (+) using the value of $W/V_{f}$ from Step 3.
Step 6.Determine scaled value of the vent area $A/V^{2/3}$
a.Calculate the unit weight of the frangible panel $W_{F}$ , if any.
b.Calculate the scaled unit weight of the frangible panel or cover $W_{F}/W^{1/3}$ .Use $W_{E}/W^{1/3}=0$ for no cover.

Step 8.Determine the scaled average reflected impulse on the element containing the vent opening with no cover according to the procedure outlined in Problem 2A-4 or on the frangible panel (cover) using the procedure of Problem 2A-6.

Step 9.Determine the scaled gas impulse from Figures 2-153 (+) to 2-164 (+)Use the values of $\bar{W}/\bar{V_{f}}$ from Step 3,$W_{F}/W^{\breve{1}/3}$ from Step 7,$A/V^{2/3}$ from Step 6 and $j_{r}/W^{1/3}$ from Step 8. Interpolate for values of $W/V_{f}$ and $j_{r}/W^{1/3}$ if required. Multiply by $\dot{W}^{1/3}$ to calculate gas impulse.
Step 10.Calculate the fictitious gas duration using Equation 2-4 and values of $P_{g}$ and $j_{g}$ from Steps 4 and 9, respectively.
